title: Redwood PLG Quickstart - Discovery with Petra Systems
questions: How long to hit first token from signup?
Can we route traffic to dedicated GPU pools?
How do you handle KMS/HSM integration?
next_steps: Alice: Send pricing and quickstart guide (includes free credits instructions)
Diego: Propose benchmark steps and sample dataset for latency/cost tests
Maya: Confirm internal pilot scope and invite infra team for technical deep dive call
action_items: Alice: Email pricing + quickstart guide by 2026-03-23
Diego: Share benchmark run instructions and example scripts by 2026-03-26
Maya: Confirm pilot participants and target API endpoints by 2026-03-25
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-21 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~44 minutes
Attendees: Alice Martin (Redwood AE), Diego Rivas (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO - Petra), Liam Park (ML Eng - Petra), Sara Gomez (Product)

[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alice from Redwood, AE on this account, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. We kicked off a quick internal sync, excited to learn how Redwood's quickstart works.
[00:14] Liam: Yep, hi all. We're mainly curious about time-to-first-token and what we need to set up for a quick pilot.
[00:20] Diego: Great, we'll walk through the PLG quickstart flow, free credits, and typical path from signup to first call. We'll also cover Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private at a high level and what triggers each path.
[00:30] Alice: Quick note, we'll share the quickstart guide and a sandbox project link after the call. The free credits policy: teams get $500 credits for first 30 days by default for PLG trials.
[00:40] Sara: Nice, that helps. Can you clarify what 'time-to-first-token' usually is? From our side infra provisioning can be a blocker.
[00:48] Diego: For Hosted API it's usually minutes after signup; you create an API key in the console and call the /v1/generate endpoint. In practice, most customers see first token in under five minutes. For Dedicated there's a prep step if you're reserving capacity — provisioning can take hours depending on commit level.
[01:10] Maya: So for a proof-of-concept we'd start Hosted, then move to Dedicated if we need isolation and throughput?
[01:15] Alice: Exactly. Hosted for quick experimentation — low friction. Dedicated when you need guaranteed throughput and data isolation, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
[01:25] Liam: On Hosted, how do you handle model variants and fallbacks? We might want cheaper LLMs for non-critical traffic.
[01:30] Diego: We have routing policies — you can route by latency or cost. There are model families and quantized variants. If capacity is constrained, Redwood will fallback to compatible variants; the platform exposes model selection and routing config. Note, sometimes the auto-transcription calls it "Redwood Dedicatedness" but it's just Dedicated.
[01:48] Sara: Ha, okay. Security is our main gating factor — SOC2, SSO, audit logs. Can you summarize the security posture for Hosted?
[01:56] Alice: Hosted is SOC 2 Type II, supports SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs. We can also enable customer-managed keys via KMS for Dedicated/Private. We'll share the security packet (link) after the call.
[02:08] Maya: Data residency? Some of our clients require EU-only processing.
[02:12] Diego: We have region controls; Hosted can guarantee regional processing depending on model availability. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployed in the desired region.
[02:24] Liam: For the quickstart, what's the SDK story? We use Python and Node.
[02:28] Alice: We have official SDKs and a simple REST interface. Quickstart examples are in the guide; a minimal python snippet and curl example get you to first token. Diego, do you want to call out a sample timeline?
[02:38] Diego: Sure. Sign up -> receive account + console access (minutes) -> create API key -> run example script (1-5 minutes). If you want to run a small benchmark we can give a script that simulates 100 concurrent requests using the hosted endpoint, but for realistic latency numbers we usually run on a representative dataset.
[02:54] Sara: Do you allow bringing your own models or custom fine-tuning?
[02:58] Diego: At the moment we host curated open models and our verified profiles. Fine-tuning is supported via model adapters for enterprise customers — for PLG quickstarts it's focused on evals and prompt engineering. You can also deploy a custom model in Private.
[03:10] Maya: Cost is another question — how transparent is the per-token billing and can we get cost estimates for our workload?
[03:16] Alice: Console gives token-level breakdown, per-route/model cost estimates, and we can run sizing to estimate monthly spend. For a pilot we can provide a cost sample for your expected request distribution.
[03:26] Liam: For the benchmark, are there optimizations like KV cache, batching, and quantization that reduce costs?
[03:32] Diego: Yes — KV caching, automatic batching, and model quantization profiles are available. The runtime picks kernels and quantization friendly paths; you can tune batching to balance latency and unit cost. We can show a config that lowered per-token cost by 30% in a recent customer POC.
[03:50] Maya: Operationally, who owns networking for Dedicated/Private? We run in a restricted VPC and need HSM/KMS integration.
[03:58] Diego: For Dedicated we manage the control plane but provide VPC peering options and KMS integrations; for Private (on-prem/VPC) you manage networking and we provide the package and guidance for HSM/KMS hookup.
[04:10] Sara: Any gotchas about latency for multi-region setups?
[04:14] Diego: Cross-region calls add RTT; we typically colocate inference near your users. Smart routing can failover to other regions but you'll see increased latency. 
[04:24] Alice: Quick question for Petra: what's your primary success criteria for the pilot?
[04:28] Maya: We're looking for sub-200ms tail latency for short chat prompts, predictable cost under $X per 10k tokens, and clear security attestations. Those are the must-haves.
[04:38] Liam: Plus an integration path with our SDKs and a way to do AB tests on model variants.
[04:42] Diego: Sounds good. We can run a pilot on Hosted with the exact prompt set and dataset, capture latency and cost, and then propose a Dedicated sizing if throughput grows.
[04:54] Sara: For the free credits, any restrictions? Is it throttled?
[04:58] Alice: Free credits are available for self-serve accounts and not for enterprise committed Dedicated. They have rate limits to prevent abuse but are sufficient for functional tests and small benchmarks.
[05:08] Maya: What's the recommended first benchmark? Are you okay if we run one during the trial period?
[05:12] Diego: Absolutely. We'll provide a sample harness that hits the Hosted API with your prompt set. We'll also include a recommended schedule for batch runs and steps to collect latency percentiles.
[05:22] Liam: When you say percentiles, do you mean p50/p95/p99?
[05:24] Diego: Yes, p50, p95, p99. The console shows these breakdowns and token-level cost.
[05:30] Sara: Can we get a short demo of the console now or is that a separate meeting?
[05:34] Alice: We can do a quick 10-minute walkthrough but Diego has a deep-dive demo deck for the infra team. Want a quick console demo now, Maya?
[05:42] Maya: Quick is fine, but we should schedule the infra deep-dive with our platform folks.
[05:46] Diego: Okay I'll flag that as a next step.
[05:50] [10:12] -- quick pause to share screen and console walkthrough -- (transcription shaky around screen clicks, some words merged)
[10:50] Diego: On the console you'll see API keys, model catalog, route configs, monitoring. Here's where you set routing policies and enable KV caching.
[11:12] Liam: I see the model list — are there size/throughput numbers per model?
[11:16] Diego: Yes, we publish verified performance profiles; they show tokens/sec on x GPU types, expected latency ranges, and memory footprint.
[11:24] Maya: For Dedicated pricing, what's the typical commit size?
[11:28] Alice: Commit sizes vary; we have monthly/annual reserved capacity options. I'll include sample pricing tiers in the follow-up.
[11:34] Sara: Any legal red flags around data usage for Hosted?
[11:38] Alice: We don't use customer data to train models on Hosted. We have contractual clauses and Data Processing Agreement language for enterprise. We'll attach the DPA and SOC2 report.
[11:46] Maya: Great. One more technical: how do you handle long context windows and KV cache eviction? We do retrieval-augmented generation and often re-use prefixes.
[11:56] Diego: The runtime manages KV cache and supports prefix caching; cache eviction is policy-driven. For RAG we typically cache embeddings and KV entries per conversation to avoid re-computation. There may be some terminology flips in the transcript — sometimes it shows KV "cash" — but it's KV cache.
[12:14] Liam: For embeddings, do you charge separately?
[12:18] Alice: Embeddings are billed per-embedding unit; the console shows both gen and embed usage.
[12:22] Sara: Can we get a sample integration snippet for our Flask backend?
[12:26] Diego: Yes we'll include a sample snippet in the quickstart repo.
[12:30] Maya: Regarding SLAs, for Dedicated what's the uptime guarantee?
[12:34] Alice: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime with latency targets on committed tiers; we'll include SLA language in the contract sample.
[12:40] Liam: Any mention of model explainability or output tracing? We need to capture request trace for auditing.
[12:46] Diego: We have tracing hooks and per-request trace IDs; console exposes traces for debugging and linking to logs. For full audit trails, Private deploys can ship logs to your SIEM.
[12:58] Sara: Ok good. Are there common integration pitfalls?
[13:02] Diego: Rate limit handling is the most common. Also ensure clients implement streaming or chunked reads to avoid front-end timeouts when you hit longer responses. We can share sample retry/backoff logic.
[13:14] Alice: Alright, recap and next steps: we'll send the quickstart guide, free credits instructions, pricing tiers, the security packet and DPA, and a benchmark harness. Diego will schedule a technical deep-dive with Petra's infra team.
[13:28] Maya: Sounds good. Can you also include example telemetry we can ingest into our observability?
[13:32] Diego: Yes, we'll include metrics endpoints and sample Prometheus integration notes.
[13:36] Sara: If we like the results, what's the typical timeline to move to Dedicated?
[13:40] Alice: Once you commit to Dedicated, provisioning and testing is typically a few days to a couple weeks depending on sizing and region. We'll walk you through that process.
[13:50] Maya: Great. Any final questions?
[13:52] Liam: One small one: do you support customer-managed encryption keys on Hosted?
[13:56] Alice: Not on standard Hosted. For customer-managed keys we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
[14:02] Sara: Thanks all, excited to try this out.
[14:06] Alice: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and set up the infra deep-dive.
[14:10] -- Meeting ends --

Notes: Transcription contains minor mis-hearings and occasional speaker attribution issues. Links shared during call: quickstart repo (link in follow-up), security packet (link), pricing tiers doc (link).
